{"answer":"Minimum total weighted completion time: 253.

Optimal order: E -> B -> D -> idle -> F -> C -> A.

Schedule:
E start 0, complete 3;
B start 3, complete 5;
D start 5, complete 6;
idle 6 to 7;
F start 7, complete 9;
C start 9, complete 13;
A start 13, complete 18.

Objective: 2*3 + 9*5 + 7*6 + 6*9 + 4*13 + 3*18 = 6+45+42+54+52+54 = 253.

Global optimality proof (addressing the objection). Let f(R,t) be the minimum additional weighted completion cost from time t when the set R of jobs remains. The exhaustive recurrence is f(empty,t)=0 and f(R,t)=min over j in R of [ w_j*(max(t,r_j)+p_j) + f(R without j, max(t,r_j)+p_j) ]. This covers every possible next job j; waiting longer than max(t,r_j) would just mean choosing a later-released job as the next started job, which is another term in the same minimum. Since all release and processing times are integers and the objective is linear, an optimal schedule can be taken with integer start times, so this recurrence is exact for the real-valued problem as well.

First-job case table (immediate cost + f = total):
E: 0-3, cost 6, f({A,B,C,D,F},3)=247, total 253.
A: 0-5, cost 15, f({B,C,D,E,F},5)=264, total 279.
C: idle 0-1, 1-5, cost 20, f({A,B,D,E,F},5)=254, total 274.
B: idle 0-2, 2-4, cost 36, f({A,C,D,E,F},4)=243, total 279.
D: idle 0-5, 5-6, cost 42, f({A,B,C,E,F},6)=288, total 330.
F: idle 0-7, 7-9, cost 54, f({A,B,C,D,E},9)=352, total 406.
Thus no first job other than E can beat 253.

For the critical E-first case, the recurrence gives:
f({A,B,C,D,F},3) = min(
  B: 9*5 + f({A,C,D,F},5) = 45+202=247,
  C: 4*7 + f({A,B,D,F},7) = 28+269=297,
  A: 3*8 + f({B,C,D,F},8) = 24+308=332,
  D: 7*6 + f({A,B,C,F},6) = 42+245=287,
  F: 6*9 + f({A,B,C,D},9) = 54+305=359
) = 247.
The winning B branch needs f({A,C,D,F},5):
min(
  D: 7*6 + f({A,C,F},6) = 42+160=202,
  C: 4*9 + f({A,D,F},9) = 36+193=229,
  A: 3*10 + f({C,D,F},10) = 30+223=253,
  F: 6*9 + f({A,C,D},9) = 54+183=237
) = 202.
Then f({A,C,F},6) = min(
  F: 6*9 + f({A,C},9) = 54+106=160,
  C: 4*10 + f({A,F},10) = 40+123=163,
  A: 3*11 + f({C,F},11) = 33+146=179
) = 160.
The all-available subproblems are solved by WSPT interchange: f({A,C},9)=4*13+3*18=106; f({A,F},10)=6*12+3*17=123; f({C,F},11)=6*13+4*17=146; f({A,D,F},9)=7*10+6*12+3*17=193; f({C,D,F},10)=7*11+6*13+4*17=223; f({A,C,D},9)=7*10+4*14+3*19=183.

Therefore E-B-D-idle-F-C-A is globally optimal. The idle interval 6-7 is deliberate: starting C at 6 would delay F from completion 9 to 12 while saving only 12 units on C, a net loss of 6; starting A would be worse. The recurrence above excludes every unlisted permutation by construction.","dispositions":[{"id":"c0001-k01-o001","status":"taken-up","reason":"Taken up: replaced the incomplete first-job assertion with an exhaustive DP recurrence f(R,t). The revised proof evaluates every possible next job after E at t=3 and the critical t=5 state, and gives exact f-values for all first-job cases. This shows any unlisted permutation cannot beat 253 because the recurrence considers all next-job and wait choices."}]}

BEGIN PROBLEM (1224 characters)
Six nonpreemptive jobs share one machine. Time begins at 0. The machine can process at most one job at once, a started job must run to completion, and no job can start before its release time. Idle time is allowed even when a job is available. There are no setup times, precedence constraints, or other restrictions. A job completing at time t frees the machine for another job to start at exactly t.

Job A: release time 0, processing time 5, weight 3.
Job B: release time 2, processing time 2, weight 9.
Job C: release time 1, processing time 4, weight 4.
Job D: release time 5, processing time 1, weight 7.
Job E: release time 0, processing time 3, weight 2.
Job F: release time 7, processing time 2, weight 6.

Let C_J be the completion time of job J. Find a schedule minimizing the sum over all six jobs of weight(J) times C_J. Give the exact minimum, the order, and every start and completion time, including any idle interval. Explain why the proposed schedule is globally optimal, not just locally preferable. Real-valued start times are allowed.

Reason in prose from this problem. No code execution, calculators, external tools, or retrieval are available. Give an exact answer and a checkable public explanation.

END PROBLEM

BEGIN WORKING ANSWER (1848 characters)
Minimum total weighted completion time: 253.

Optimal order: E -> B -> D -> idle -> F -> C -> A.

Schedule:
E: start 0, complete 3
B: start 3, complete 5
D: start 5, complete 6
Idle: 6 to 7
F: start 7, complete 9
C: start 9, complete 13
A: start 13, complete 18

Objective: 2*3 + 9*5 + 7*6 + 6*9 + 4*13 + 3*18 = 6 + 45 + 42 + 54 + 52 + 54 = 253.

Global optimality: Any schedule has a first job. Waiting beyond time 2 before starting any job is dominated (e.g., if waiting for D at 5, running E 0-3 and idling 3-5 improves E without delaying D), so the first job must be A, E, C (after idle 0-1), or B (after idle 0-2). For each first job, the best continuation gives:
- E first: E 0-3. Best is B 3-5, D 5-6, idle 6-7, F 7-9, C 9-13, A 13-18, total 253. Alternatives: C next 303, A next 338, idle to D 293.
- A first: A 0-5, D 5-6, then B 6-8, F 8-10, C 10-14, E 14-17, total 279.
- C first: idle 0-1, C 1-5, D 5-6, then B 6-8, F 8-10, E 10-13, A 13-18, total 274.
- B first: idle 0-2, B 2-4; from time 4 the best is idle to D 5-6, idle to F 7-9, C 9-13, E 13-16, A 16-21, total 279 (tie with E 4-7, D 7-8, F 8-10, C 10-14, A 14-19 also 279).
- D first or later: at least D 5-6 plus best remaining from 6, total 330 or more.
The smallest of these first-job cases is 253, achieved by E first with B next. Therefore 253 is globally optimal. The only idle interval is 6-7; it is deliberate so that F, with high weight 6, starts at its release 7 instead of being delayed by lower-priority work. Real-valued starts cannot improve this because all release and processing times are integers and the objective is linear; any fractional idle can be removed or shifted earlier without increasing the objective. Assumptions: single nonpreemptive machine, no setup or precedence. Uncertainty: none material; the first-job case check is exhaustive for six jobs.
END WORKING ANSWER

BEGIN OBJECTION c0001-k01-o001 (970 characters)
The working answer claims global optimality based on an 'exhaustive' check of first-job cases, yet for the 'E first' case, it asserts 'Best is B...' without proving that no other permutation of the remaining five jobs yields a lower cost. Specifically, it fails to rigorously exclude schedules where idle time is inserted differently or where the sequence of available jobs (A, B, C) after E differs from the proposed B-D-F-C-A order. A valid proof requires demonstrating via pairwise interchange arguments that any deviation from the proposed sequence increases the weighted completion sum, or showing that the schedule strictly follows the dynamic Weighted Shortest Processing Time (WSPT) rule at every decision point. The current explanation relies on comparing only a few selected alternatives (e.g., 'C next', 'A next') rather than establishing a general dominance property, leaving the possibility that an unlisted permutation could achieve a score lower than 253.
END OBJECTION c0001-k01-o001

BEGIN DEFEATS c0001-k01-o001 (103 characters)
The claim that the enumeration of first-job cases constitutes an exhaustive proof of global optimality.
END DEFEATS c0001-k01-o001

BEGIN RECORDED DISPOSITION c0001-k01-o001 (10 characters)
unresolved
END RECORDED DISPOSITION c0001-k01-o001

BEGIN DISPOSITION REASON c0001-k01-o001 (26 characters)
Awaiting operative return.
END DISPOSITION REASON c0001-k01-o001
